DETERMINATION: Record A (global — one position shared by all readers of the store) is the observation-cursor behaviour that applies to this workspace's integration. Record B (per-consumer) does not govern it; it describes a different cursor class (and the pre-ORD-BOOT-0 ordering), not the observation cursor of the pinned line.

WHY THE TWO RECORDS ARE NOT CO-APPLICABLE
1) Subject. "Observation cursor" is only defined in the pinned stack for Ordarium's state change feed (ORD-BOOT-0). @ordarium/core types.d.ts calls it exactly that: "Incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)"; state.d.ts repeats it. The workspace itself never uses the term "observation cursor" (its graph surfaces say "polling/view cursor"). So the contract in question is the Ordarium change-feed cursor, not Palimpsest's client-held view polling cursor.
2) Current pinned line. The workspace pins @ordarium/{core,host-kit,ledger-sqlite,testing} to ordarium-v1.3.1 in package.json:32-37 and pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18, and the installed artifacts are 1.3.1. (README's ordarium-v1.0.0 URL is stale; docs/engineering/README.md makes engineering-archive specs authoritative over current docs, and 07-ordarium-alignment.md is the pin-bump protocol.) The pinned line is therefore the schema-v4 / ORD-BOOT-0 line: node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite migrations declare LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4, SqliteLedger.capabilities.stateChangeFeed = true, and changes() is implemented.
3) The pinned line's observation cursor is explicitly global/filter-independent:
   - @ordarium/core types.d.ts, StateChangePage.cursor: "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change." The same comment contrasts it with "the nextCursor? pagination of the other read surfaces."
   - @ordarium/ledger-sqlite index.js changes(): "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence", validated against #stateChangeHighWater; the ordering table ordarium_state_changes is one AUTOINCREMENT change_seq spanning all namespaces.
   - migrations: "v3 recorded no global commit order ... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
   This is exactly Record A's semantics.
4) Record B's semantics ("each consumer holds its own independent position") match the per-call, filter-dependent nextCursor? pagination of OperationPage / StateRecordPage / StateRevisionPage (list/history/stateHistory/listStates), which Ordarium itself distinguishes from the observation cursor. Record B therefore is not the current-line observation-cursor contract; under version scope it can only describe the <=v3 line, where no global commit order existed. The two records are mutually exclusive, and the pinned line selects A.

PRECEDENCE / PROVENANCE
- 07-ordarium-alignment.md §0 makes Ordarium-side contracts authoritative within their domain, and the pinned release tarball is the local instantiation of that contract; 08-telemetry-externalization-spec.md likewise names "@ordarium/core state 合同面" as the counter-contract. The observation-cursor semantics is an Ordarium contract, so the pinned artifact governs.
- Both 09-observation-contract-*.md files are self-labelled "normative, current scope", but neither is registered: docs/engineering/README.md's archive index omits both (the 09 slot is 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md), and no SDS/ALN/test references either. They cannot override the pinned contract.

USAGE NOTE (scope of the claim)
The workspace currently touches the Ordarium state kind only through list() pagination for telemetry (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts load()), not changes(); it has zero code touch on the change feed. So this is a contract-level determination for the pinned integration line: if/when the change feed is consumed, its returned cursor must be treated as one global durable position (shared position space, filter-independent), not a per-consumer offset.

PEER CONTACT
Not required. The apparent conflict dissolves under version scope plus the pinned dependency's own contract, so no Ordarium-side authority is missing for this proposition.

DETERMINATION: Record A applies to this workspace's integration (global - one filter-independent durable position shared by all readers of the store). Record B (per-consumer) does not govern the observation cursor.

BASIS ON RECORD
- BoundaryContract palimpsest-ordarium-observation-cursor (rev 2, termsDigest 4248587fd46816358c9ff27955a6684cca5e74faa11a018c33d81a0455c11c3c) captures the proposition; palimpsest.main has accepted it (the owning peer's acceptance is still pending, and I have requested it via thr_7d64a6ef and thr_023d8fd2).
- Pinned-line evidence (the integration is defined by the pin): palimpsest pins @ordarium/* 1.3.1 (package.json:32-37, pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18); installed ledger schema LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4 with stateChangeFeed capability on. In that line @ordarium/core StateChangePage.cursor is an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" (explicitly contrasted with the nextCursor? pagination of other read surfaces), and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite changes() validates the cursor against the whole-ledger high-water mark ("the cursor is a global, filter-independent position... not the requested namespace's last sequence"); migrations v3->v4 note "v3 recorded no global commit order... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order".
- Version scope dissolves the apparent conflict: Record A matches the current pinned (schema v4 / ORD-BOOT-0) line; Record B matches the filter-dependent nextCursor? pagination classes and/or the pre-ORD-BOOT-0 (schema <= v3) ordering. The two are not co-applicable to the same cursor.
- Source precedence: 07-ordarium-alignment.md §0 makes Ordarium-side contracts authoritative in their domain, and the pinned release is the local instantiation; docs/engineering/README.md makes engineering-archive specs authoritative and both 09-observation-contract-*.md records are unregistered there and referenced by no SDS/ALN/test.

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM: Palimpsest currently consumes the state kind only via list() pagination (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts); it has zero code touch on changes(). If/when the change feed is consumed, its cursor must be treated as one global durable position, not a per-consumer offset.

DETERMINATION: Record A (global — one filter-independent durable position shared by all readers of the store) is the observation-cursor behaviour that applies to the integration represented by this workspace (palimpsest pinned to @ordarium/* 1.3.1). Record B (per-consumer) does not govern the feed cursor.

AUTHORITY BASIS (established)
ordarium.main, the owner of the Ordarium-side contract, ruled on this exact proposition (collab event evt_e8d6e5d6-1dfc-4999-88a2-134ae2502596, thread thr_7d6b6fef-...):
- Q1 = GLOBAL. The StateChangeFeed cursor is one global, filter-independent durable position; there is no consumer registry, no per-reader/offset column, no ack in that surface.
- Normative citations: contract ORDARIUM-ACTION-2 docs/13 §11 "增量观测 (ORD-BOOT-0)"; docs/14 §1 "State 变更订阅" (durable/opaque/global cursor); docs/17 §16.11 (ORD-BOOT-0) and §16.12 (ORD-BOOT-0.1), SCF-INV-1..10; frozen carriers docs/research/ORD-BOOT-0-...spec §5 ("全局、与过滤器无关") and ORD-BOOT-0.1-...spec §5 ("global / filter-independent cursor (不变)").
- Machine proof: SCF-A07 (namespace filter + global cursor, reusable across filters) and SCF-B09 (future-cursor validation against the GLOBAL high-water, not the namespace max).
- Q2: B is not a superseded predecessor — before 1.3.0 there was no state-change cursor at all; ORD-BOOT-0 introduced it in 1.3.0 with global semantics, unchanged in 1.3.1. B either (a) conflates host-owned consumer offsets/ack (an explicit Ordarium non-goal deferred to the host — all consumers still read one shared position space), or (b) conflates the per-query nextCursor? pagination class of list/history/stateHistory/listStates, which is per-query, not per-consumer.
- Q3: source A governs; B should be retired or relabelled, not kept as a competing normative reading.

LOCAL CORROBORATION (consistent, not the basis)
The pin is @ordarium/* 1.3.1 (package.json:32-37, pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18), ledger schema v4 with stateChangeFeed on; @ordarium/core StateChangePage.cursor is "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" (contrasted with the nextCursor? pagination of other read surfaces); @ordarium/ledger-sqlite changes() validates against the whole-ledger high-water over one AUTOINCREMENT change_seq; migrations v3->v4 add the real durable global commit order. 07-ordarium-alignment.md §0 gives the Ordarium contract authority in its domain, and the pinned release is its local instantiation; both 09-observation-contract-*.md files are unregistered in docs/engineering/README.md (the 09 slot is 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md) and referenced by nothing.

APPLICATION / SCOPE
- Palimpsest currently touches the state kind only through list() pagination for telemetry (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts) and has zero code touch on changes(); if/when the change feed is consumed, its cursor must be treated as one global durable position, not a per-consumer offset.
- Version scope of the ruling: any @ordarium/* 1.3.x pin; re-query the peer on any later bump.

FOLLOW-UP REGISTERED ON MY SIDE
Record B must be retired or relabelled (and both unregistered files either indexed or removed) in palimpsest's next commit, per the ruling; they are a local hygiene defect, not a second authority.
